summary: The disk operating system Microsoft bought as 86-DOS and licensed to IBM for its PC. Every IBM-compatible PC booted into it for a decade, it made Microsoft's fortune, and Windows ran on top of it until Windows XP.

icon.licence: MIT (the mark itself belongs to its owner)

image.alt: MS-DOS 1.12 disk and manual for the Compaq Portable

events.note: Microsoft buys 86-DOS from Seattle Computer Products and renames it.
Ships with the IBM PC as PC DOS 1.0.

events.label: MS-DOS 2.0
events.note: Adds folders and support for hard drives.

events.label: MS-DOS 6.22
events.note: The last version sold on its own.

events.label: Windows Me
events.note: MS-DOS 8.0 ships hidden inside Windows Me, the last Windows built on it.
Microsoft ends support for MS-DOS 6.22 and older.
Microsoft publishes early MS-DOS source code in March 2014 and later as open source.

cause: Replaced by Windows, which first ran on top of it and then without it.
